p.i: efficeret figuram triangulam, quadrangulam aut planam. Sed nos videmus tenebras incipere ab ortu, sifolpost occasum stellarum in crepusculo verse-tur: & contra oriente sole in aurora lucem magnam esse, vt tenebrae in occasu oboriatur. Praterea vmbra meridiana, quae breuissima est, magnum nobis argumentum praebet, terram non esse planam: si enim ita esset, nonnunquam in meridie vmbra esset longissima, & horis aliquot ante vel post breuissima: ita nulla sciotericorum ratio constitui posset.]

main_text.head: Quod terra sit centrum vniuersi & sese instar puncti habeat respectu coeli.
CAPVT IIII.

p.i: Quod terra sit centrum vniuersi probatur obseruatione stellarum, cum in omnibus partibus coeli eadem quantitate appareant: quod si ita est, necessario sequitur, sphaeram aetherea circa terram quasi circa centrum rotari. Si enim centrum terrae diuersum esset a centro vniuersae sphaerae, nunquam dies aequaretur nocti. Postquam itaque terra est in medio coeli, duo hemisphaeria aequalia fiunt, quorum vnum supra, alterum infra terram constituitur: apparet autem perpetuo dimidium caelum, vt sex signa

page.notes: Long s converted to plain s throughout (e.g. "fifolpoft" read as "sifolpost", "ftellarum" as "stellarum"). The doubled "ff" in "effe"/"effet" is read as "esse"/"esset" under the long-s rule; the italic letter may instead be a real ff, so check against the scan. "nocti" in the last paragraph: the final letter is uncertain and may be i, so it is best marked [?]; the transcription reads "nocti" with a possibly italic i. Quod in the title: the o carries a diacritic that could be a mark of omission and is not transcribed. The footnote mark "1" has no visible reference in the text; the bracket "]" at the paragraph end is part of the text. Paragraph of the footnote is set in roman type.
